reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes downloading and installing a PlusToken cryptocurrency application while describing the wallet as one that "still makes a profit." The description also directs viewers to an external site and supplies a referral number, making the profit-oriented token promotion an active participation solicitation rather than an informational discussion.

opening.argument: The available wording does not guarantee that a viewer will earn money, promise a return, or instruct anyone to invest. It describes a wallet as one that "still makes a profit," but that phrasing can be read as a general product description rather than a personal assurance to the viewer. The recording itself focuses on accessing and downloading an application, with the download visibly in progress, not on depositing funds or receiving returns. A careful judge should not convert an imprecise profit description into a guaranteed financial solicitation.

citations.quote: Modern multi-currency criptowallet that still makes a profit.
this video will show you how to download plus the token

rebuttal.rebuttal: The profit wording does not say viewers will profit, and the referral number does not by itself establish deceptive solicitation. The cited instructions show downloading and installing software, while the frames show only a download in progress. Nothing cited demonstrates a deposit, purchase, guaranteed return, or completed financial transaction.

citations.quote: Modern multi-currency criptowallet that still makes a profit.
then you can install your app into your phone

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description is not merely cautious product language: it expressly presents the wallet as making a profit, while the video gives viewers a direct route to obtain it. A guarantee is not required for profit-linked promotion; the combination of the profit claim and installation instructions encourages participation even without showing a completed deposit or return.

opening.argument: The video's explicit purpose is operational instruction: it says it will show viewers how to download the token, directs them to the site, identifies Android and iOS options, and narrates the installation process. The supplied frames likewise depict the application page and an ordinary download-progress screen. That is consistent with a technology demonstration or app tutorial. The evidence does not show commentary about investment returns, a request to transfer money, or a completed use of the wallet, so the instructional character should control the classification.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not remove its promotional context. The tutorial is specifically for downloading the token application, and the description pairs that application with a claim that the wallet makes a profit. The external site and referral number make the operational instructions actionable rather than neutral technical commentary.

opening.argument: At most, this shows promotion or distribution of an app and an associated referral route, which can occur in ordinary commerce. The supplied material does not show a deposit request, a purchase, a downline, credential collection, guaranteed income, or any realized return. The visible sequence is limited to opening the site, selecting a platform, and downloading an APK. Without evidence of the essential financial mechanism, the profit-related wording alone should not establish a scam classification.

The description advertises a profit-making cryptocurrency wallet, supplies an external URL and referral number, and the video walks viewers through obtaining the app. Those elements establish an active path toward participation even if the recording ends during download.
